jobs.prompt:
test(cpp): fuzz the JSON, URL and regex engines of uos::rt and fix crashes

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
This branch contains `cpp/gateway/`: a finished module-for-module C++20 port of the repository's first-party TypeScript runtime (`src/`, `serve.ts`, `lib/jev_compaction/`): 325 modules (`cpp/gateway/include/uos/**` + `cpp/gateway/src/**`), a JavaScript-semantics runtime layer `uos::rt` (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`), and 436 test files (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`, each a standalone binary using the tiny harness `include/uos/rt/test.hpp`). The TypeScript is the behavioural ORACLE: the port reproduces its behaviour including quirks; expected values in tests were recorded from Bun 1.4.0. Everything so far was built and tested ONLY on one Linux/AArch64 host with GCC 12.2, Boost 1.81, -O0. Your runner is the first other machine to build it.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/PORT-NOTES.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/TESTING.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OPEN-STAGES.md`. Notes on them:
- PORTING.md's "Host safety" section and the rule "compile only through tools/unit.sh" exist because the authors' machine is a production server. They do NOT apply on your disposable runner: use the compilers directly, build in parallel (`-j4`), use sanitizers and extra build directories freely. All other porting rules (fidelity to the TypeScript, naming, no stubs, the coroutine rules) apply.
- `cpp/gateway/tools/unit.sh`, `tools/env.sh`, `tools/build.py` and the CMake presets are tied to host-specific absolute paths (an SDK under /home/codex/..., a toolchain directory). Do not depend on them as they are. Each test's exact source list is in its leading `// Links:` comment or in the registry `cpp/gateway/tests/LINKS.txt`; `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test file>` prints the resolved list (read the script; adapt if it assumes host paths). Every `src/rt/*.cpp` links into every test binary.
- Compiler flags the port is held to: `-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion -Werror -DBOOST_JSON_NO_LIB -DBOOST_CONTAINER_NO_LIB -DBOOST_SYSTEM_NO_LIB -I cpp/gateway/include -I cpp/gateway`, linking Boost.JSON, Boost.Container, OpenSSL (ssl, crypto), pthread; some runtime pieces `dlopen` libsqlite3, libz, libbrotlidec, libzstd (the working tree may be mid-migration to linking them directly: follow what the sources do).

YOUR MACHINE: a fresh GitHub-hosted Ubuntu x86_64 runner (4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, about 14 GB disk), with sudo and network access. Install what you need: a recent GCC (g++-14 or newer; GCC 12 has a coroutine miscompile, do not use it), Clang, CMake, Ninja, `libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev`, Boost >= 1.83 with Boost.JSON (the distribution package is fine; the port also targets Boost 1.92), optionally mold and ccache. Bun 1.4.0 is the pinned JavaScript runtime for oracle checks (`bun install --frozen-lockfile` is allowed on the runner); when you need to know what the TypeScript does, run it under bun rather than guessing.

RULES
- Fix root causes. Never weaken, skip or delete a test or an expected value to make it pass; expected values come from Bun. If you believe an expectation is wrong, prove it by running the TypeScript under bun and say so in your report.
- Stay inside the OWNED paths listed below. A defect outside them is REPORTED, not fixed: append it to your findings file with the failing command, the first error lines and your diagnosis.
- Do not edit anything under `.github/` (the push of your branch would be rejected). Do not edit `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` (the TypeScript) or anything under `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`.
- The runner's environment contains a model gateway token: never print it, never write it or any other credential into a file.
- Your work is pushed when you stop, even on timeout: keep the tree in a committable state, write your findings file EARLY and update it as you go, and do not leave build directories, binaries, corpora over 1 MB or downloaded archives inside the repository checkout (build under /tmp).
- Do not reformat files you did not need to change.

FINAL MESSAGE (also write it to your findings file): what you built and how (exact commands), what passed and failed with real counts, every source change with its reason and evidence, everything you could not finish, and defects found outside your owned paths.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these)
- `cpp/gateway/src/rt/json.cpp`, `src/rt/url.cpp`, `src/rt/regex*.cpp`, `src/rt/regex_internal.hpp`, `include/uos/rt/json.hpp`, `url.hpp`, `regex.hpp`
- `cpp/gateway/fuzz/json.cpp`, `fuzz/url.cpp`, `fuzz/regex.cpp`, new files `fuzz/dict/*.dict`, `fuzz/corpus/json/`, `fuzz/corpus/url/`, `fuzz/corpus/regex/`, and additive edits to `fuzz/support.hpp`, `fuzz/targets.json`, `fuzz/seeds.json`
- `cpp/gateway/tests/rt/json_test.cpp`, `url_test.cpp`, `regex_test.cpp` (add regression cases)
- `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-fuzz-json-url-regex-20261117c.md`

TASK
Fuzz three hand-written parsers of untrusted input and fix what breaks: `uos::rt` JSON (`src/rt/json.cpp`: `jsonParse`, `jsonStringify`), URL (`src/rt/url.cpp`: `URL` parsing with and without a base, setters, `URLSearchParams`) and the ECMAScript regular-expression engine (`src/rt/regex*.cpp`: pattern compilation and matching).
The tree already has libFuzzer harnesses and seeds written by an earlier agent that never ran them for long: `cpp/gateway/fuzz/json.cpp`, `fuzz/url.cpp`, `fuzz/regex.cpp`, `fuzz/support.hpp`, `fuzz/targets.json`, `fuzz/seeds.json`, `fuzz/seed.py`, `fuzz/run.py`, `fuzz/corpus/`. Read them, make them build on this runner with Clang (`-fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined -O1 -g`), improve them where they are shallow (for regex: fuzz the pattern AND the subject, both flag sets, all API entry points: test/exec/matchAll/replace/split; for URL: structured inputs for base + relative + setter sequences; for JSON: parse then stringify then re-parse and assert a fixpoint), and add a small dictionary per target.
Run each target for at least 60 minutes of wall time on all cores (e.g. `-jobs=4 -workers=4`, `-max_len` suited to the target, `-timeout=10`, `-rss_limit_mb=2048`). Three classes of findings, all to fix at the root in the engine source: (1) memory errors and undefined behaviour; (2) hangs and super-linear blow-ups beyond what JavaScriptCore itself exhibits on the same input (check with bun before calling something a bug: the regex engine deliberately mirrors JSC's backtracking behaviour and has a documented memory cap, see `docs/rt/regex.md`); (3) DIFFERENTIAL mismatches against Bun: add a differential mode that, for a sample of generated inputs (a few thousand per target), compares the C++ result with what Bun 1.4.0 returns for the same input (`JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` result or SyntaxError message; `new URL(input, base)` fields or throw; RegExp construction error text and exec results) and treat every mismatch outside the limits documented in `docs/rt/values.md`, `web.md`, `regex.md` as a defect.
For every fixed defect add the minimised input as a regression case in the existing test file (`tests/rt/json_test.cpp`, `tests/rt/url_test.cpp`, `tests/rt/regex_test.cpp`) and keep all existing cases passing in a normal build. Commit minimised crash inputs under `cpp/gateway/fuzz/corpus/<target>/` (small files only; do not commit the grown corpus).
Deliverable besides the fixes: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-fuzz-json-url-regex-20261117c.md`: executions and coverage reached per target, every finding with its minimised input (hex if not printable), cause and fix, and the differential mismatch statistics.

NOTE: a small local change may land upstream in `appendQuoted` in `src/rt/json.cpp` (an ASCII fast path replacing `if (!shortEscape(unit)) continue;` with `if (unit >= 0x20 && unit != '"' && unit != '\\') continue;`). Apply that same one-line change yourself first if it is not already present, verify `tests/rt/json_test.cpp` still passes, and keep it.
